transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep hearing the bank and bill collectors talking about me, like they’re sending me messages that I’ve ruined everything, even when no one else hears anything. It is just so clear to me, but my wife swears there is nobody there. I'm just really scared and didn't know what else to do.

During this time, have you also had a period of several days where you felt unusually high or energized, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or had racing thoughts? Or have you mostly just been hearing these voices and feeling scared?

No, I've never had any times where I felt high or energized; it has actually been the exact opposite. I feel completely drained and heavy all the time, like I'm trying to move through thick mud. Mostly, I've just been feeling deeply down and terrified by those voices telling me I've ruined my family.
Did the voices start only after you became deeply depressed, and do they happen only when your mood is very low? Or have they also happened during times when you were not feeling depressed?

The voices only started after I had been feeling deeply depressed and worthless for several months because of our money problems. I never experienced anything like this back when I was still working and feeling like my normal self. They only happen when I am feeling this low.

Therefore the current candidate list narrows to [F32.3].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms: persistent depressed mood, marked low energy/psychomotor heaviness, worthlessness, and mood-congruent auditory hallucinations. Psychotic symptoms began after months of depression and occur only during periods of very low mood, supporting major depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic disorder or bipolar disorder. Mania/hypomania was explicitly denied.
